title: Oakridge Systems — Hosting & Portability decision framework
summary: Initial discovery for migrating Oakridge's LLM stack off Azure OpenAI / self-hosted vLLM. Focus on compatibility, eval parity, private deployment constraints (VPC/KMS), and timeline for pilot. AE+SE present. Next steps: provide pricing for dedicated, security docs, and run parity benchmark with their test-suite.
next_steps: Redwood to share Dedicated and Private pricing matrix and an outline of pilot sequence (Maya) — by 2027-05-20
Oakridge to send eval prompt set and sample traffic profile (Ethan) — by 2027-05-21
Schedule 90-min technical deep-dive with infra team to review VPC/KMS specifics (Liam + Marta) — target week of 2027-05-24

Liam Chen | Prepare compatibility checklist for vLLM/TGI and provide recommended quantization profiles | 2027-05-21

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-18
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (scheduled 60)
Recording: yes
---
[00:00] Maya Ruiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, I'm the AE on this account. With me is Liam Chen, our solutions engineer. How are you all?
[00:08] Priya Nair: Hi Maya, hi Liam. Good thanks. Priya here.
[00:11] Ethan Park: Ethan. Afternoon.
[00:13] Marta Silva: Marta from InfoSec, hi.
[00:15] Maya Ruiz: Great. Quick agenda — we want to understand your current stack, success criteria for a migration, compliance constraints, and then outline next steps for a parity pilot. Does that sound right?
[00:25] Priya Nair: Yeah that's the goal. We're evaluating whether to keep using Azure OpenAI for production and a self-hosted vLLM cluster for burst, or move to a unified provider. We're worried about cost creep and having two different runtimes.
[00:37] Maya Ruiz: Totally. Can you walk us through the current architecture and any non-negotiables?
[00:42] Ethan Park: Sure. Right now our inference pipeline is: customer requests hit an API gateway, then we route to Azure OpenAI for safety-filtered responses. For heavy batch jobs and some offline scoring we spin up a vLLM cluster on k8s with TGI for an open model. We do custom quantization and run a slightly trimmed KV cache with Redis. We — uh — also use internal prompt templating.
[01:03] Liam Chen: When you say TGI, is that the Hugging Face TGI server or a custom wrapper?
[01:09] Ethan Park: It's a TGI-based container, yes. We have a shim so we can fall back between TGI and the vLLM endpoints. But the serialization between the two and the tokenization differences are giving us drift in A/B tests.
[01:22] Maya Ruiz: Drift meaning eval mismatch on your prompt set?
[01:25] Ethan Park: Exactly. Same prompt, different completions and slightly worse scores on our meaning-preservation metrics when we fall back to vLLM.
[01:32] Priya Nair: And the business problem is we want deterministic SLA behavior and predictable cost per 1k tokens. Managing both vendors is operationally expensive.
[01:40] Maya Ruiz: Understood. Liam, any quick notes on common causes of parity issues here?
[01:44] Liam Chen: Yeah. There are a few: tokenizers, sampling defaults, temperature/seeding, and hidden model config like repeated ngram penalty or presence penalties. Also how KV cache is handled — vLLM's continuous batching can change prompt trimming behavior. Quantization can shift outputs if not done carefully.
[02:03] Marta Silva: From security side, we have to ensure any hosted solution meets SOC 2 and we need audit logs and KMS integration for keys. We also have data residency constraints for EU customers.
[02:13] Maya Ruiz: Good to know. Redwood supports SOC 2, we have region controls, and for Private deployments we can integrate with customer KMS and HSM. We'll include the SOC 2 and architecture diagrams in the docs pack.
[02:23] Priya Nair: What about RBAC and multi-tenant separation? We can't have token leakage between teams.
[02:28] Liam Chen: Our Dedicated offering provides tenant isolation at the GPU pool level and RBAC in the console. For Private, you manage the control plane in your VPC and we support SAML/SSO, fine-grained roles, and audit trails.
[02:40] Ethan Park: Good. On quantization, we did 4-bit with a custom QAT pipeline which seems to destabilize when we change libraries. Do you recommend specific quantization profiles?
[02:50] Liam Chen: We typically recommend per-workload profiling. For many LLaMA-family weights, an 8-bit FP or 4-bit with GPTQ-inspired kernels maintains parity for ranking/semantic tasks. We can share a recommended matrix — some of which depends on whether you're doing classification, generations, or embeddings.
[03:06] Priya Nair: Ok. Can you talk through the pilot flow — how would we test parity across OpenAI, vLLM/TGI, and Redwood?
[03:13] Maya Ruiz: Short answer: we run your prompt suite against a pinned model on Redwood Hosted and Redwood Dedicated/Private (if you want private), capture token-level latency/costs, and compare outputs via your eval metrics. Liam will detail the instrumentation.
[03:23] Liam Chen: We'll spin a small dedicated pool with the same model variant and sequence-length profile you provide. We'll also run a vLLM instance with identical model weights and quantization settings if you can provide those artifacts. Then we compute delta on your benchmarks — BLEU/ROUGE-style or semantic similarity, plus unit cost delta.
[03:40] Ethan Park: How do you handle tokenizer differences? That's been a big headache.
[03:44] Liam Chen: We'll normalize tokenization by running a canonical tokenizer step in the eval harness before comparing outputs; and where possible we'll use the same tokenizer binary. If model artifacts differ (e.g., different byte-pair merges) we'll note that.
[03:55] Priya Nair: Timeline — we want to decide in 6 weeks whether to run a 3-month pilot. Is that realistic?
[04:00] Maya Ruiz: Yes. Typical cadence: discovery (this call), then a benchmark pilot scoping (1 week), then a 2–4 week parity benchmark, then decide. So 6 weeks to commit to pilot is doable.
[04:10] Marta Silva: For Private deployment, are there on-prem packages? We cannot send certain logs off-network.
[04:15] Liam Chen: We have an on-prem distribution that runs fully behind your firewall. Control plane optionality — you can keep the control plane on our managed control plane in a dedicated VPC, or run a customer-managed control plane. Logs can be retained on-premise. We also support forward-only audit exports.
[04:31] Ethan Park: Cost: can you ballpark differences between staying with Azure + vLLM ops vs Redwood Dedicated?
[04:36] Maya Ruiz: I can provide a pricing matrix, but at a high level: Dedicated gives predictable committed throughput and lower per-token unit cost at scale, whereas Hosted is pay-as-you-go. Many customers saw 20–40% unit cost improvements when they moved high-throughput workloads to Dedicated with appropriate batching and caching. We'll share case studies.
[04:55] Priya Nair: And resiliency — do you have automatic fallback to cheaper model variants during overload? We need graceful degradation.
[05:02] Liam Chen: Yes. Smart routing policies can fall back to smaller quantized variants and we can keep a warm warm pool for those. You can set latency SLOs and cost thresholds.
[05:12] Maya Ruiz: Back to parity: what acceptance criteria do you want to use for parity pass/fail?
[05:17] Priya Nair: We have a primary semantic-similarity threshold 0.92 on our internal metric, latency under 250ms p50 for our simple prompts, and token-cost within 15% of our current blended cost.
[05:29] Ethan Park: Also need to check failure modes — e.g., truncated responses, double-tokenization, and hallucination increase under quantization.
[05:38] Liam Chen: We'll include those checks in the harness. We also recommend measuring regression on a holdout prompt set to detect unseen degradation.
[05:48] Priya Nair: For compliance, some regulators ask for deterministic output logs. Is that feasible?
[05:54] Marta Silva: We need immutable logs with retention policies and ability to export for audits.
[05:59] Liam Chen: We can produce tamper-evident audit logs and integrate with your SIEM via secure export. For Private/on-prem we can keep all logs behind your infrastructure.
[06:10] Ethan Park: About model versions — can we pin a model? We need stable reproducibility across deployments.
[06:15] Maya Ruiz: Absolutely. Redwood supports model pinning and rollout policies for canary/A-B. You get consistent versions across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
[06:24] Priya Nair: What about stateful sessions and KV cache portability? Our product uses long contexts and offloaded KV caches in Redis.
[06:33] Liam Chen: We support prefix and KV caching with configurable eviction. For Dedicated we can configure co-located Redis or our in-memory caching subsystem. The important bit is cache serialization format — we'll map that in the compatibility checklist.
[06:46] Ethan Park: Any gotchas moving from vLLM + custom kernels to Redwood runtime?
[06:51] Liam Chen: The runtime kernels differ; in some workloads you'll get better throughput but you might need to adjust batch sizes. Also some custom GPU kernels in your stack could require re-profiling. We'll provide a migration playbook.
[07:03] Priya Nair: Can we run a small benchmark inside our environment first? Meaning run Redwood agents with an on-prem connector?
[07:10] Maya Ruiz: For sure — we offer a Private runner you can deploy for pilot that talks to our instrumentation so we can collect telemetry. That lets you keep data local while we observe.
[07:20] Marta Silva: If we go Private, what's the support SLA? We need enterprise on-call and a runbook for incidents.
[07:26] Maya Ruiz: Enterprise support is available with 24x7 on-call, dedicated CSM, and an escalation path. We'll include the SLA doc.
[07:34] Ethan Park: One practical thing — tokenization differences have caused prompts to shift because of invisible control characters. Can you normalize whitespace?
[07:42] Liam Chen: The harness applies canonical normalization steps; we also diff on semantic embeddings so whitespace-only differences won't cause a parity fail.
[07:51] Priya Nair: Regarding the plateaued tests — when we tried open models the diversity increased. Can Redwood help tune decoding params?
[07:58] Liam Chen: Yes — we'll iterate on sampling parameters and temperature, and we can do guided generation with constraints if you need determinism.
[08:07] Maya Ruiz: Quick check — is the primary motivation cost, reliability, or operational consolidation?
[08:12] Priya Nair: All of the above but consolidation is top. We want one serving plane that gives us predictable costs and fewer operational headaches.
[08:18] Ethan Park: Also to reduce manual effort of maintaining the vLLM fleet.
[08:21] Marta Silva: And compliance.
[08:23] Maya Ruiz: Good. We'll tailor recommendations across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Dedicated is often the sweet spot when teams need committed throughput and isolation without full on-prem.
[08:33] Liam Chen: For the parity run, here's what we need from you: prompt set, model weights or exact model name, quantization settings, sample traffic distribution (sequence length histogram), and a list of holdout prompts.
[08:43] Ethan Park: I can get that. We'll need to scrub any PII from the logs.
[08:47] Marta Silva: We'll only provide anonymized datasets for the benchmark.
[08:50] Maya Ruiz: That works. We'll document the exact data handling and sign an addendum if necessary.
[08:55] Priya Nair: One more thing — what's the experience like during a failover? If a region goes down can requests be routed to a different region with the same model?
[09:02] Liam Chen: Yes — multi-region routing is supported. You can pin primary region, and fallback region, and the runtime will route according to your policy. There may be a small latency delta but it's seamless.
[09:12] Ethan Park: For the pilot, do you have standard metrics dashboard?
[09:16] Maya Ruiz: Redwood Console shows per-route latency, token cost, model-level traces, and regression alerts tied to the eval harness. We'll give you access during the pilot.
[09:26] Priya Nair: Great. On the commercial side, are there minimum commitments for Dedicated?
[09:31] Maya Ruiz: Yes, Dedicated is typically a monthly reserved capacity commitment; we have flexible tiers. We'll include the options in the pricing matrix.
[09:38] Ethan Park: Is there a migration support package to help with model weight conversion?
[09:42] Liam Chen: We offer migration services — converting weights, recommended quantization, and an ops runbook. That can be scoped into the pilot or as separate professional services.
[09:52] Priya Nair: Ok that's helpful.
[09:54] Maya Ruiz: Shall we recap next steps?
[09:56] Priya Nair: Yes please.
[09:57] Maya Ruiz: Action items — Maya will send pricing and pilot runbook, Liam will send compatibility checklist and suggested quantization table, Ethan will provide anonymized prompt set and traffic histogram, Marta will confirm InfoSec questionnaire answers. We'll aim to reconvene for a technical deep-dive the week of the 24th.
[10:18] Ethan Park: Sounds good.
[10:19] Marta Silva: I'll ping calendar invites once I check schedules.
[10:21] Priya Nair: Thanks Maya, Liam. Looking forward to the docs.
[10:24] Maya Ruiz: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by Friday with the initial packet.
[10:28] Liam Chen: Thanks. Bye.
